# From the foot Jacobian and joint torques, how should WORLD and LOCAL_WORLD_ALIGNED be chosen?

> **Current answer:** Maintainer notes that the original post's WORLD Jacobian is applied at the world origin, which seems to be attached to LF_FOOT; it is not the intended center of the foot. LOCAL_WORLD_ALIGNED is applied at the LF_FOOT frame, with axes aligned to the world frame. The author used LOCAL_WORLD_ALIGNED and confirmed the force values are more reasonable. The original thread did not verify the rest of the assumptions regarding 3×3 matrix extraction, pseudoinverse, and peak torque mapping, so only the reference frame correction is confirmed, and results cannot be called strictly maximum contact force.

## Key terms

- Local-world-aligned frame (LOCAL_WORLD_ALIGNED) (局部世界对齐坐标系)
- Foot-frame Jacobian (足端雅可比)
- Contact-force mapping (接触力映射)
- Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse (摩尔-彭若斯伪逆)

## Problem and symptoms

- Why is one force component significantly larger than expected when estimating contact force from the foot Jacobian using peak joint torques?
- Using the WORLD frame, extracting a 3×3 Jacobian, and performing a pseudoinverse on J^T results in at least one x/y/z force component that is significantly larger than expected.

## Environment

- Pinocchio Python 2020; FreeFlyer quadruped; q0 is a unit base quaternion; LF_FOOT Jacobian.

## Priority diagnostics

- First, check if the Jacobian's reference frame matches the required point and axis direction.

## Possible causes

- The WORLD frame corresponds to the world origin, and is not centered and world-aligned at the LF_FOOT.

## Attempts

- The author changed the reference frame of computeFrameJacobian from WORLD to LOCAL_WORLD_ALIGNED.

## Effective fixes

- Use LOCAL_WORLD_ALIGNED when the contact force mapping requires the center of the foot and world-aligned axes.

## Result

- The author confirmed the force values are more reasonable after changing the reference frame.

## Limitations

- The thread did not prove the 3×3 matrix is invertible, nor did it verify the pseudoinverse, other leg coupling, floating base balance, or friction constraints.
- A more reasonable number does not equate to a strictly maximum feasible contact force.

## Safety notes

- Force torque limits and contact feasible region deployment must be verified under complete floating base dynamics and friction constraints before deployment.
